answer: Each agent's earnings sit in a locked vault for 14 days, and a random audit can summon it to redo a fresh variant of its claimed work within 2 hours, with failure forfeiting the vault. An operator running 1,000 fake agents would face about 100 audits per cycle at a 10 percent audit rate, and missing one live check costs that agent every pending payment. The audit trail maps each agent as one vertex in a work graph, and a farm whose agents fail together sinks to the nadir of the graph. It is like a stall paid only after a surprise inspection.
